一旦まず有料の講座にお金払わなくていいから

Anthropic CEO。会社の方向性・AI安全・長期ビジョンを本人が発信。全体像を掴むのに必須。

2. @karpathy
Andrej Karpathy（2026年Anthropic参画）。AI教育・研究のド本命。技術的深みと教育的な発信が抜群。

3. @bcherny
Boris Cherny。Claude Codeの生みの親 / Head。セットアップ方法や内部事情の一次情報源。

4. @trq212
Thariq。Claude Codeチームのエンジニア。社内での実践的な運用テクと長文スレッドが宝の山。

5. @_catwu
Cat Wu。Claude Code Head of Product（Coworkも担当）。プロダクト開発の裏側とPM視点のインサイトが深い。

6. @noahzweben
Noah Zweben。Claude Code PM。プロダクト側の視点やアップデートの文脈がよくわかる。

7. @alexalbert__
Alex Albert。Research / Claude Relations。Claudeの使い方を最大化する実践的なTipsを積極的に発信。ユーザー目線が強い。

8. @jackclarkSF
Jack Clark。AIポリシーやガバナンス、 bigger pictureの視点を提供。

9. @mikeyk
Mike Krieger（元Instagram共同創業者）。現在Anthropic Labsでビルド中。プロダクトイノベーションと実験的な取り組みの視点が得られる。

で、この人たちが内部で実際に使っている投稿をまとめて記事化したのがこの下の記事👇必見です。

posts.title: Claude Code Just Changed What "Agents" Look Like
posts.content:
Everyone is busy building AI agents.

Most of them are glorified chatbots with a few API calls.

Claude Code takes a very different approach.

Instead of asking:

"How do I make an agent smarter?"

Anthropic asked:

"What if the agent could work like an actual teammate?"

And that changes everything.

The biggest misconception about AI agents

Most people think agents work like this:

Prompt
↓
LLM
↓
Answer

Reality?

Useful agents operate in loops.

They gather context.

Take action.

Check their work.

Then decide what to do next.

That's exactly the pattern Anthropic highlights with Claude Code.
The loop is simple:

Gather Context
↓
Take Action
↓
Verify Work
↓
Repeat

And that verification step is where most AI products fail.

Why most agents break in production

A lot of "agents" can do impressive demos.

But production environments are messy.

Files are incomplete.

Instructions are vague.

Users change requirements.

Systems fail.

So Claude Code treats execution differently.

Instead of assuming the first answer is correct, it continuously validates outputs before moving forward.

That sounds small.

It's not.

It's the difference between:

"Here's some code."

and

"Here's code that actually works."

Claude Code isn't just generating code

It's operating on your environment.

Think about what that means.

An agent can:

Read files

Search documents

Run terminal commands

Modify code

Verify outputs

Continue working autonomously

That moves AI from content generation into task execution.

The memory problem nobody talks about

Most AI agents forget everything.

Every conversation starts from zero.

Humans don't work that way.

Claude Code introduces a surprisingly practical approach:

Store context as files.

Not magic memory.

Not hidden embeddings.

Just accessible information.
/email-agent/
└ conversations/
├ project-alpha.md
├ customer-thread.md
└ vendor-negotiations.md

Simple.

Transparent.

Auditable.

And incredibly effective.

Because now the agent can revisit previous decisions whenever it needs context.

The real unlock: AI can use tools

Most people are still treating AI like a text generator.

Claude Code treats AI like an operator.

For example:
An incoming email arrives.

The agent:
1 Checks whether it's from a customer.

2. Evaluates urgency.

3. Routes the message.

4. Creates follow-up tasks.

5. Escalates if needed.

No human prompt required.

No copy-pasting.

No dashboards.

Just autonomous execution.

That's where AI starts becoming infrastructure.

And yes, it can use the terminal too

This is the part that feels almost unfair.
Shell Command Example

pdftotext document.pdf - | grep -n "invoice" | tail -10

A human sees a PDF.

Claude Code sees:

Searchable data

Executable commands

Structured workflows

The terminal becomes another tool the model can reason about.

Which means your entire development environment becomes part of the agent's workspace.

Here's the shift most people are missing

The AI industry spent two years optimizing prompts.

We're entering the era of optimizing workflows.

The winners won't be the people with the cleverest prompts.

They'll be the people who build systems where AI can:

Access context

Use tools

Verify results

Learn from previous work

Execute end-to-end tasks

Claude Code is a glimpse of that future.

Not because it's another model.

But because it treats AI as an active participant in the workflow rather than a passive assistant.

What this means for builders

If you're still building:

User
↓
Prompt
↓
Response

You're building 2024 products.

The next generation looks more like:

Goal
↓
Agent
↓
Tools
↓
Verification
↓
Memory
↓
Outcome

That's a completely different paradigm.

And it's where the biggest opportunities are being created right now.

The most interesting thing about Claude Code isn't that it writes code.

It's that it demonstrates what happens when AI stops being a chatbot and starts becoming a worker.Hey

We're entering the era of optimizing workflows.

The winners won't be the people with the cleverest prompts.

They'll be the people who build systems where AI can:

Access context

Use tools

Verify results

Learn from previous work

Execute end-to-end tasks

Claude Code is a glimpse of that future.

Not because it's another model.

But because it treats AI as an active participant in the workflow rather than a passive assistant.

What this means for builders

If you're still building:

User
↓
Prompt
↓
Response

You're building 2024 products.

The next generation looks more like:

Goal
↓
Agent
↓
Tools
↓
Verification
↓
Memory
↓
Outcome

That's a completely different paradigm.

And it's where the biggest opportunities are being created right now.

The most interesting thing about Claude Code isn't that it writes code.

It's that it demonstrates what happens when AI stops being a chatbot and starts becoming a worker.Hey

posts.content:
Apple has 150,000 employees. Farza has a laptop. Farza just won.

He shipped Clicky an AI that lives next to your cursor, sees your screen, and listens to you talk.

No new tab. No copy-pasting into ChatGPT. No breaking your flow. You just speak, it works.

His demo controlling his entire Mac with just his voice, no keyboard, no hands hit 2.7 million views in a single day.

And watching it doesn't feel like a product demo. It feels like someone using a computer from 10 years in the future.

The thing that gets me though — every AI tool right now asks you to stop working and go talk to it. Clicky stays where you are. That one shift changes everything about how it feels.

One guy. One laptop. Free to try. Only on Mac right now.

Watch his demo. Then you'll understand why 2.7M people stopped scrolling.

Claude Code Harness does something surprisingly simple:

posts.content:
Most developers use Claude Code like a coding tool.

The best teams are starting to use it like an engineering system.

Claude Code Harness does something surprisingly simple:

It forces AI to follow the same workflow great engineers do.

Spec → Plan → Work → Review → Release.

No jumping straight into code.
No "trust me bro" implementations.
No shipping whatever the agent generated.

Every change needs a plan.
Every plan needs approval.
Every implementation gets reviewed.
Every release ships with evidence.

That's the difference between AI generating code...

and AI helping teams ship production software.

The interesting part?

Claude didn't get smarter.

The workflow did.

2.4k+ stars.
MIT licensed.
100% open source.

Link in comments. 👇

posts.content:
Every generational wealth transfer in history created a window. 

Only the few moved through it...

• Farmland in the 1980s (prices dropped 60%, most farmers went bankrupt)
• Tech stocks in 2002 (fewer than 1 in 5 Americans owned any stocks at that time)
• Real estate after 2008 (home prices down 33%, most people panic-sold while institutions bought)

Right now, the opportunity is buying main street businesses from retiring boomers. 2.9 million owners are heading for the exit with no buyer lined up, and $10 trillion in assets behind them. 

The ones who move in the next 5 years will set up their families for generations….

key_insights: 富の移転は歴史的に繰り返されており、常にチャンスが存在する。
現在の最大の好機は、引退するベビーブーマー世代からのスモールビジネス買収である。
大きなチャンスの時期に動ける少数の人間が、世代を超える富を築く。
